names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 mai, «Sfântul Apostol Andronic și soția sa, Iunia».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the body of the Охридски пролог's first entry for 17. мај ст. ст., „свету Јунију, помоћницу Андроникову“, with the accusative resolved to the nominative the same body gives three words later, „Са светом Јунијом“ → Јунија; света is not a rank and „помоћницу Андроникову“ is a relation and not a name. **This is the one form in these three days that is not read off a heading**, the Prologue giving her none, and it is a copied script form all the same — not a transliteration. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: no folder in the corpus holds this form in any language.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 mai — «Sfântul Apostol Andronic și soția sa, Iunia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps her on, and it is plainly the same person: Paul's kinswoman and fellow prisoner of Romans 16.7, kept with Andronicus on one page that carries both as head names. **The page counts her among the Seventy**, whose common feast it puts on 4 January; that is a common commemoration and not a second Greek feast, and it is recorded here and nothing is moved. **Its couplet for her prints a date that is not a feast and nobody is moved on it**: «Ἰουνία τέθνηκε μηνὶ Μαΐῳ, Ὃς πρῶτός ἐστιν εἰσιὼν Ἰουνίου» — Junia died in the month of May, which is the first to come in before June — which is a conceit on her name and the month, not a day; and the joint verse below it reads «Ἑβδομάτῃ δεκάτῃ θάν' Ἰουνίη Ἀνδρόνικός τε», on the seventeenth died Junia and Andronicus, which agrees with the listing. **The joint apolytikion is copied**, naming both; the page's second hymn is the bare common of apostles and is left. **No year is printed**, so no `dates` object is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.05.2026 (17. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети апостол Андроник.“ — „спомињући и свету Јунију, помоћницу Андроникову … Пострадаше обоје за Христа, и тако примише двострук венац: и апостолства и мучеништва.“

attestations.note: **A ROW OWED OUT OF ANOTHER SAINT'S HEADING, as `laodicius-the-jailer`'s was on the Julian 13 May.** The Prologue gives her no heading of her own: the day's first entry is headed „Свети апостол Андроник.“ and she is in its body, named four times — „свету Јунију, помоћницу Андроникову“, „Са светом Јунијом он успе да многе приведе Христу“, „Имађаху обоје благодатну силу чудотворства“, „Пострадаше обоје за Христа, и тако примише двострук венац“. **The body narrates her apostolate, her wonderworking and her martyrdom**, which is the test that owes a row and not the merely-mentioned that does not; so the `text` quotes the heading whole, as the contract requires, and then the clauses that are hers. She is on the same menologion 17/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry. **The Prologue takes the helper reading, not the wife reading.** „помоћницу Андроникову“ — his helper — is doxologia's own „ajutătoarea sa“ and not its day line's „soția sa“, his wife, and this folder's life already holds both readings as the source prints them; **the Prologue is a second book for the helper and nothing is decided on it.** **New here**: that she shared the gracious power of wonderworking, demons driven out and every sickness healed, and that the crown was double for her too. **`paul-the-apostle` IS ADDED to `related`**: Romans 16:7, which the Prologue cites, names her with Andronicus as Paul's kinsfolk, and this folder's life already quoted the verse without the row. `types` untouched. No `locations` — the Prologue names Pannonia for Andronicus and nothing for her. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Sfinţilor Apostoli rugaţi pe milostivul Dumnezeu ca să dea iertare de greşeli sufletelor noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Apostoli Andronic și al soției sale Iunia», Glasul 3 — the one troparion the page prints for the two together, in the short form of the common of apostles

english.text: Holy apostles, entreat the merciful God to grant our souls forgiveness of our sins.

hymns.text: Δυὰς φωτοειδής, ἱερῶν Ἀποστόλων, καὶ κήρυκες Χριστοῦ, ἀνεδείχθητε κόσμω, τοὶς πάσι κατασπείραντες, τὸ τῆς χάριτος κήρυγμα, ὅθεν σήμερον, ἠμᾶς πιστῶς εὐφημοῦμεν, ὢ Ἀνδρόνικε, καὶ Ἰουνία θεόφρον, Χριστὸν μεγαλύνοντες.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Τὸν τάφον σου Σωτὴρ, on the page of Άγιοι Ανδρόνικος και Ιουνία οι Απόστολοι — the joint hymn of the two; the page gives it no tone line of its own, so none is recorded

english.text: A pair full of light, holy apostles and heralds of Christ, you were shown forth to the world, sowing among all the preaching of grace; and so today we faithfully praise you, O Andronicus and God-minded Junia, magnifying Christ.
